.. to also handle the `o[str + "constant"]` case, i.e. where the rhs is
a string constant.

findings.title: Swapped Parameter Types in AddRhsIsStringConstant Builtins Cause Type Confusion
findings.message: The newly introduced TF_BUILTINs `AddRhsIsStringConstantInternalizeWithVector` and `AddRhsIsStringConstantInternalizeTrampoline` declare their parameters with swapped types: `left` is typed as `Parameter<String>` when it should be `Parameter<Object>` (since for the kRhsIsStringConstant variant, the left operand is an arbitrary value), and `right` is typed as `Parameter<Object>` when it should be `Parameter<String>` (since it is the constant string). This is a copy-paste error from the existing kLhsIsStringConstant builtin where the string IS on the left. The swapped types cause V8 to incorrectly treat any object passed as the left operand as a String type. When the left operand is a Growable SharedArrayBuffer (GSAB, i.e., `is_shared()=true && is_resizable_by_js()=true`), downstream code that calls `JSArrayBuffer::byte_length()` triggers the DCHECK `!is_shared() || !is_resizable_by_js()` in `src/objects/js-array-buffer-inl.h:36` because the GSAB object is incorrectly processed through string code paths.
findings.suggestion: Swap the parameter type declarations so that `left` is `Parameter<Object>` (arbitrary left operand) and `right` is `Parameter<String>` (the constant string on the rhs). This matches the calling convention for the kRhsIsStringConstant variant where only rhs is guaranteed to be a String.

ground_truth.root_cause: Copy-paste error from the existing `kLhsIsStringConstant` builtin (where `left` is correctly `Parameter<String>`) to the new `kRhsIsStringConstant` builtin, without inverting the parameter type declarations to match the new variant's semantics. In the kRhsIsStringConstant case, it is `right` (not `left`) that is the guaranteed String constant.
